title_original: PHP2Shell: Log4Shell at AI Speed — A CISO’s Perspective
description: When the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities became public, my thoughts went back to Log4Shell.  Five years ago, Log4Shell showed how difficult it can be to respond to a critical vulnerability in software used across countless applications and services. PHP2Shell presents a similar challenge. The technical details are different, but the need to quickly understand where you’re exposed and take action is very familiar.  I believe we should expect more incidents like this. AI is making it possible to discover vulnerabilities in widely used software at a speed and scale we haven’t seen before. title_original: PHP2Shell Update: One in ten organizations impacted as Europe bears the brunt
description: Two critical vulnerabilities in PHP, the programming language behind a large share of the world’s websites, online stores and internet services, are being actively targeted. Since details of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, known as PHP2Shell, leaked ahead of planned disclosure, 10% of organisations worldwide have been impacted (“impacted” means exploitation attempts, we have no way of knowing if the attack has been successful), according to Check Point Research. Hourly activity peaks at midnight, when fewer security teams are watching. Government institutions in the Netherlands and Finland have taken some of their websites offline as a precaution.
